newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds hold steady, spread over bunds narrows.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds hold steady, spread over bunds narrows.

text.p: Irish government bonds shrugged off weakness in other European markets to hold steady in afternoon trade on Monday, allowing the yield spread between German and Irish 10-year bonds to narrow, dealers said.
"Germany has come back and we have held our own and this has helped the differential to narrow. We have outperformed by about 35 pence," one dealer said.

Bunds suffered as investors traded out of Germany into other European bonds after the Dublin ECOFIN meeting and amid worries about President Boris Yeltsin's health. Jitters ahead of Tuesday's U.S. FOMC meeting did not help sentiment either.
By 1537 GMT, the eight percent Irish 10-year bond was at 105.65 to yield 7.05 percent against 105.70 at the close.
Dealers said the spread over the 10-year bund breached 100 basis points, falling to 97 basis points from 102 late last week.

But traders said that yield spreads between Germany and Ireland had narrowed in by about 25 basis points over the last fortnight and were unlikely to move much further until there was further news on economic and monetary union (EMU).
Irish progress could also be hampered by supply with the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) tempted to take advantage of market strength and issue stock, dealers said.
Attention tomorrow will focus on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
Dealers said a rate rise of 25 basis points was already priced into the market but if the Fed opted for a larger, 50-basis point move, it should help U.S. Treasuries to rally.
